title: Soccer: Goal, Teams, and Ball
summary: Explore how soccer works and why teamwork matters. Meet famous football players from several countries and learn about their achievements.

items.prompt: Can you name a famous soccer player?
What do you enjoy about team sports?

blocks.title: Part 1: The Main Idea of Soccer
paragraphs: Soccer, also called football, is a game between two teams. Each team usually has eleven players. Players move the ball mainly with their feet. They try to put the ball into the other team’s goal, the large net at the end of the field. One goal gives one point. The team with more goals wins. If both teams have the same score, the result is a draw.

images.alt: A player kicks the ball toward a large goal net while teammates support the attack.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: The Main Idea of Soccer

items.prompt: How does a soccer team score a point?
items.answer: A soccer team scores a point by putting the ball into the other team’s goal.

blocks.title: Part 2: Time and Basic Rules
paragraphs: A normal soccer match has two halves of 45 minutes. The referee can add extra minutes when play stops. Most players cannot touch the ball with their hands or arms. The goalkeeper can use their hands inside the penalty area, the large box near the goal. A foul happens when a player breaks a rule, for example by kicking another player instead of the ball.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: Time and Basic Rules

items.prompt: Which player can use their hands inside the penalty area?
items.answer: The goalkeeper can use their hands inside the penalty area.

blocks.title: Part 3: Different Positions
paragraphs: Players have different jobs, called positions. Goalkeepers protect the goal. Defenders try to stop attacks. Midfielders connect defense and attack. Forwards try to score goals. Some players change how a position works. German goalkeeper Manuel Neuer often moved far from his goal to pass the ball or stop an attack early. People call this active style a sweeper-keeper style.

images.alt: A goalkeeper, defenders, midfielder, and forward show their different jobs on a real pitch.

items.prompt: What is the main job of a forward?
items.answer: The main job of a forward is to attack and try to score goals.

blocks.title: Part 4: Teamwork Wins Matches
paragraphs: Great players need a strong team. Players pass the ball, move into open spaces, and help one another. Argentina showed this teamwork at the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Captain Lionel Messi scored two goals in the final. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez also made an important late save. Argentina and France drew 3–3, and Argentina won the penalty shootout. One star was important, but the whole team created the victory.

items.prompt: Why was Argentina’s 2022 World Cup victory a team success?
items.answer: It was a team success because Messi scored, Martínez made an important save, and the players worked together.

blocks.title: Part 5: Famous Women Players
paragraphs: Women’s soccer has many famous stars. Marta, from Brazil, scored 17 goals in FIFA Women’s World Cup matches, a World Cup record. She is known for skillful movement and close control of the ball. Homare Sawa captained Japan when the team won the 2011 Women’s World Cup. She scored five goals in that tournament and received the Golden Boot as its top scorer.

items.prompt: What did Homare Sawa and Japan achieve in 2011?
items.answer: Homare Sawa captained Japan to victory in the 2011 Women’s World Cup and was the tournament’s top scorer.

blocks.title: Part 6: What Makes a Player Famous?
paragraphs: A player can become famous through skill, records, trophies, and exciting moments. Brazilian star Pelé won the men’s World Cup three times: in 1958, 1962, and 1970. Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal has won five Ballon d’Or awards, which honor an outstanding player. These famous football players have different styles, but both scored many goals and inspired fans around the world.

images.alt: Original women footballers celebrate on a sunlit pitch, one lifting a trophy and one keeping close control of the ball.
